2026-07-04 Korea

Korea Day 1-2

The flight to Korea

Starting the trip with (supposedly) Vietnamese food at the airport.
I was happily surprised that AC got Korean side dishes in their food. Then I ate it... They should be ashamed of calling this Korean.
Had the cutest baby in front of me. He kept looking between the seats at me and making faces.
Finally here! 21 hours after leaving my apartment 😅

Bus to Hotel

I love this! Some lanes are colored (matching the road signs) to tell you where to go. Toronto needs this!
Seriously. You can't escape Canada 😂. This Tims is a 3 min walk from my hotel. Apparently Seoul has like 20!
Tons of restaurants near the hotel. I ordered the small pork ribs ... 😂. Really good just a touch spicier that I wanted then.

DMZ Tour

Our tour guide, Julie, was very knowledgeable and hilarious. I feel like we got a free stand-up comedy show with the tour!

Heading to meeting point

Korean breakfast approved
Korean pastry also approved

Lake Bridge

Mountains in the area make this a very scenic area!

Observatory

From this point until the end of the tour, photography is limited.

3rd Tunnel

This is the closest you can get to the MDL (Military Demarcation Line) today. Crazy to think that this was dug by hand with very basic tools.

Not much more to share without photos of the tunnel, but it was quite the exercise (coming back up). The entrance to the tunnel is very steep!

Lunch (Buffet)

This is (from my social media feed) what I expected meals look like in Korea. Lived up to the expectations!

Interesting Facts

Warning: This is my recollection of the guide's commentary. Believe it at your own risk (or fact check).

  1. North Korea and South Korea are still technically at war. The Korean War ended in 1953 with an armistice, not a peace treaty. The two countries are still in a state of war.
  2. 4 tunnels have been discovered that North Korea has dug to try to invade South Korea. They were between 1974 and 1990. There is no clear evidence of how long it took to dig them, or if those are all, but it is clear from remains that there was intent to invade South Korea. 30000 soldiers could have come through each tunnel with their weapons in 1 hour. Not clear how long they took to build, but with the technology at the time, it would have taken a long time.
  3. The UN has a presence in the DMZ. They have a small base in the area and are responsible for monitoring the armistice. Because of this, tourism at the DMZ is also regulated by the UN. So decisions around photography and access have been changed recently by them due to the current tensions in the area. In fact, you could tour the JSA (Joint Security Area) before, but now you can't.
  4. Both still provoke each other in other ways. They blast speakers with propaganda (North Korea) or K-pop (South Korea) at the DMZ. NK also jams signal and sends trash balloons to the South.
  5. Having been to South Korea on its own makes it very unlikely you could ever visit North Korea (already hard in the first place).

Myeongdong

This was the meeting place for the tour so I was dropped off here after the tour, so I took advantage of the time to explore the area. It is a very busy shopping area with lots of street food and shops. Korean skincare is no joke. Tons of skincare-related shops everywhere!!
